analysis.investment_thesis: Aurionpro is a recovering mid-cap banking-tech player with a clean balance sheet (D/E 0.02) and decent near-term earnings momentum, but its sprawling product portfolio, low promoter ownership, and acquisition-heavy capital deployment make it difficult to underwrite a durable moat. At 25x trailing P/E with a 14.6% net profit CAGR and 5.7% revenue CAGR over nine years, the price is fair but not compellingly cheap for the quality on offer.
key_strengths: Near debt-free balance sheet (borrowings collapsed from INR 154 Cr in FY20 to INR 30 Cr in FY25) gives financial flexibility
Accelerating revenue/profit since FY22 turnaround — revenue up 2.3x and net profit up 2.5x in three years to FY25
Banking/fintech software carries moderate switching costs; OCF positive all 5 of the last 5 years
key_risks: Promoter stake is only 26.88% — low skin-in-the-game is a yellow flag on management alignment
Acquisition-driven growth: investing CF -INR 421 Cr in FY25, -INR 203 Cr in FY24; equity doubled in two years via capital raises — dilutive and hard to value
FCF conversion is poor — FY25 FCF just INR 62 Cr against net profit of INR 188 Cr (33% conversion), as capex jumped to INR 95 Cr
red_flags: Net loss of INR 192 Cr in FY21 and revenue collapse from INR 710 Cr (FY16) to INR 374 Cr (FY21) — a decade of volatility that is inconsistent with the 'predictable earnings' I require
Total equity surged from INR 498 Cr (FY23) to INR 1,606 Cr (FY25) via aggressive capital raises — signals M&A-driven rather than organic compounding
Business spans banking software, data centres, smart cities, AI labs, trade finance, and supply chain — far outside my circle of competence and lacking the focus I expect in truly great businesses
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Aurionpro ticks some basic boxes — minimal debt, positive operating cash flow, and a visible recovery in profitability since FY22. ROCE of 18.1% and ROE of 15.3% are acceptable but only marginally clear my 15% hurdle, and the nine-year revenue CAGR of just 5.7% tells me this business spent the better part of a decade going nowhere. The current growth narrative is real but young — I would need at least five consecutive years of clean, organic earnings growth before I felt comfortable calling it durable.

What concerns me most is capital discipline. The company raised large amounts of equity in FY24–25 and ploughed INR 624 Cr into investments over two years; that kind of M&A pace often destroys as much value as it creates, and the poor FCF-to-profit conversion ratio (33% in FY25) suggests earnings quality is not high. With promoters holding barely 27%, I do not see the owner-operator mentality I prize. At a forward P/E of ~17x the price is not obviously expensive, but with a complex, unfocused portfolio and a chequered history of losses, I am not being paid enough to bear the uncertainty. I would watch from the sidelines.
